# Trebell Code

> Trebell Code is Trebell's flagship product: a free desktop workspace for AI coding agents. The current release is 2.0.1, for Windows 10 and 11 (x64).

## Product

- Trebell Code: https://code.trebell.dev/
- Current release: 2.0.1, Windows 10 and 11 (x64) installer

- Updates: from 2.0.0 on, the app checks the public releases repository for new versions; an update downloads and installs only when the user chooses.

## What it does

Trebell Code is a desktop coding workspace around coding agents: files, terminal, Git and pull requests, worktrees, previews, a browser panel, projects and environments. Every turn keeps an activity card that shows what it did, such as a command's exit code and duration or an edit's diff.

## Harnesses

- Trebell Native: Trebell's own agent harness, with its own model and tool loop calling model APIs directly. OpenAI is the default provider.
- Codex: runs the Codex CLI the user has installed.
- Claude Code
- OpenCode: OpenCode 1.x and OpenCode 2.
- Cursor
- Grok Build
- Antigravity: runs with a Gemini API key from Google AI Studio.
- Muse Code: Meta's coding agent, new in 2.0; sign in with `muse login`.

Each of the seven external agents runs as its real harness, with its own models, sign-in, approvals and updates.

## What's new in 2.0

- Muse Code is a new harness: its replies, reasoning, commands and file edits stream into the thread, its approvals and questions come to Trebell's own card and dialog, and Usage shows its 5-hour and weekly windows.
- OpenCode 2 is supported beside OpenCode 1.x.
- Each harness brings its own model list, options and default; a reopened thread resumes on the model it used; a harness's thinking shows as a collapsed Thinking row.
- A redesigned interface: one design across the app, the same top bar on every page, and replies as GitHub-style Markdown with tables and copyable code blocks.
- Every turn shows what it did, and a turn that failed or was stopped before it replied says how and why.
- Trebell Native streams replies on OpenAI (code-change turns are checked before the answer), can look at images in the workspace, and waits out network drops instead of failing the turn.
- Harness updates from Settings.
- Lighter on the machine: fewer background processes, less CPU and GPU while typing and streaming, and large threads open with much less disk and database work.

## Intended users

Trebell Code is built for software developers and engineering teams using AI coding agents on real codebases, especially where provider choice, reproducible execution, verification, and cost visibility matter.

## Business model

Trebell Code is free for developers. Trebell plans a paid team infrastructure layer with shared policy, usage and cost controls, managed execution environments, auditability, and administration.

## Benchmarks

Trebell Native was compared with Codex using the OpenAI API, with the same model and settings on both: gpt-6-luna, max reasoning, fast service tier, hosted web search off. Tasks were fresh (never used before), and an independent verifier graded each run. Cost is API-equivalent, compared on the tasks where both got the same verifier result.

- SWE-bench Multilingual, 156 fresh tasks: Trebell Native resolved 125, Codex using the OpenAI API resolved 124. Native's cost was 0.819x (95% bootstrap interval 0.75-0.90), 18% less.
- Terminal-Bench 2.0, 78 fresh tasks: both resolved 62. Native's cost was 0.721x (0.58-0.87), 28% less.
- Terminal-Bench Pro 1.0, 40 fresh tasks: Trebell Native resolved 22, Codex using the OpenAI API resolved 21. Cost was statistically level (0.929x, 0.80-1.08).

These results compare Trebell Native with Codex using the OpenAI API under the settings above; read them as that comparison, not as a claim about every harness or setup.
